manual.p: When Pike encounters an error that it can't handle, or finds something suspicious in a program, you may get an error message or a warning. An error message is a piece of text that Pike prints in order to inform you of a problem that has occurred, and that prevents the program from continuing. A warning is like an error message, but is just given as information of a possible problem.
Your program can print its own warnings and error messages, but this chapter is about those that Pike itself prints when it reads and examines your program.

manual.out: ex3.pike:17: Warning: An expression type mixed cannot be assigned to a variable of type int.
manual.p: Warnings and error messages are not printed on the standard output, but on the standard error output. Even if you re-direct the output from a program, the standard error output is usually printed on the screen.

manual.p: Error messages are always printed, and will cause the program to terminate. By default, warnings are not printed. They are turned off by default, and you have to turn them on.

It is usually a very good idea to turn on warnings, at least during program development. Why would you not let the computer help you find the bugs in your program?
